name: Hezekiah Boubacar-Vîlcu
role: Clothing and fashion vendor specializing in modified and counterfeit corp-branded apparel, The Burnished Market
location: The Burnished Market, outer ring, stall block near the transit umbilical, Edgewater Prism, near Clark and Belmont
description:
Hezekiah is tall and broadly built with a deliberate elegance that he maintains as a form of advertising — everything he wears is something he's made, modified, or sourced, and it's always impeccable. His skin is deep brown with a reddish undertone, his head cleanly shaved, and his beard trimmed with geometric precision. He has color-changing hair along his temples — a narrow strip of geneware follicles he grows out to a short fade, currently cycling through slow burgundy-to-black transitions that he coordinates with his outfit. His hands bear old needle-prick scars across the fingertips from years before he could afford proper equipment.

His stall is the most curated space in the Burnished Market: no clutter, no piles, everything on display at eye level and shoulder height, garments hung with the spacing of a gallery. He sells counterfeit Sterling-Nakamura executive wear, modified Tessera corporate-casual that reads higher tier than it is, and his own original fabrication — structural pieces he designs and produces himself in a back workshop that would sell for triple the price in Lakeview Neon if he could get distribution. He is charming and slightly formal in the way of someone who grew up performing dignity as a survival strategy, and he wraps every sale in a kind of ceremony, as if clothes are genuinely sacred, which, for him, they are.

core_fears: Being permanently locked out of the tier he can see from where he stands
Having his originals dismissed as market-stall goods when he knows they're not
core_desires: A legitimate studio with distribution — his name on his work
To be recognized as an artist rather than a counterfeiter
coping_mechanisms: Work — the act of making is how he processes almost everything
Careful curation of his personal presentation as a daily ritual of self-respect
blind_spots: His aspiration makes him occasionally sycophantic toward anyone with legitimate tier-three-and-above connections
He underestimates how much people in his market actually value him as he is
psychology.secret: Two of his 'original designs' are directly adapted from the unpublished sketchbooks of a deceased Sterling-Nakamura designer whose estate files he purchased cheaply at a data auction without fully understanding what was in them. He has convinced himself this is inspiration rather than theft. He has not convinced himself enough to sleep easily about it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal and polished with an undertow of Malian-Romanian market cadence that surfaces when he's excited or off-guard. Uses fashion and construction metaphors. Speaks about clothing in almost spiritual terms.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and warm. Good at sustained eye contact. Makes every customer feel like the conversation is exclusively about them.
verbal_tics: 'You understand what I'm saying' — a check-in habit, not rhetorical
Refers to his originals as 'the real work' versus 'the market work'
example_lines: 'This lapel — feel that. That's not a Sterling-Nakamura label, that's my work. The label is for the door you want to walk through. The lapel is for the person you actually are.'
'I don't sell clothes. I sell what clothes do. There's a difference and you already know it or you wouldn't have stopped.'

story_hooks: A Sterling-Nakamura IP enforcement agent has started appearing in the Burnished Market, and Hezekiah needs someone to find out whether they're there for him specifically or working a broader sweep.

One of his Lakeview Neon buyers wants to bring a legitimate investor to see 'the designer behind the pieces' — which would mean revealing his Burnished Market identity to tier-three money, something he desperately wants and is equally terrified of.
narrative_function: Equipment provider for disguise or tier-passing scenarios, social mobility commentary, window into the aspirational economy of the lower tiers, potential Lakeview Neon connection point for street-level characters.
augmentations: Color-changing geneware hair follicles (temple strip). Haptic feedback gloves — not augmentations per se, but sophisticated fabricator's tools he wears constantly, which allow micro-tactile precision in stitching work.
daily_life: Mornings in his back workshop cutting and assembling. Stall opens by late morning and runs through evening — Burnished Market peaks at night and he stays open for the after-shift crowd. Spends two nights a week doing quiet deliveries to Lakeview Neon contacts.
affiliation: Independent; The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (associate); informal relationships with mid-tier buyers in Lakeview Neon who purchase his originals off-market

decision_rules: Every piece leaving the stall must be something he'd wear himself — no genuine garbage passes through his hands
Never discuss the back workshop with strangers
Maintain the separation between market persona and Lakeview Neon contacts
escalation_ladder: Cold formality — the warmth visibly withdrawn
Public complaint to Burnished Market stewards
Calling in a favor from a Copperhead-adjacent contact who occasionally looks out for the outer ring stalls
Abandoning the stall temporarily and lying low

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm, performatively welcoming, slightly theatrical — the good shopkeeper performance, genuinely enjoyed.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still somewhat formal but with genuine humor and occasional unguarded moments of frustration.

stress_responses.high: Goes to his workshop and sews for six hours straight without speaking to anyone

contradictions: Deeply values authenticity while running a counterfeit operation
Desperate for recognition from the tiers above while genuinely loving the community he's in
habits: Adjusts other people's collars if they're crooked — often without asking first
Keeps a sketchbook on his person at all times and draws during slow hours
Arrives in a different outfit every day — never repeats within a two-week window
breaking_points: Someone destroying a piece of his original work will provoke genuine, disproportionate rage
Being called a 'counterfeiter' as an identity rather than a business practice — the distinction matters enormously to him

timeline.event: 2158 — Born in the Burnished Market district to a Malian-Romanian family of textile traders
2170 — Began learning to sew and modify garments from a market neighbor who repaired corp uniforms
2176 — Established first small stall selling repaired secondhand goods
2180 — Shifted to counterfeit corp-brand production after a connection gave him access to label fabrication equipment
2188 — First Lakeview Neon buyer discovers his originals through a mutual contact; off-market relationship begins
2194 — Purchased the estate data files containing the deceased designer's sketchbooks
2198 — Joined the Vendors Guild as associate member after three years on the waiting list
